text:
alex: Customer on Dedicated reported intermittent 500s + huge tail latency (~5-10s) for /v1/generate. Happened ~3x in last hour. They included request_id: req_3a9f7b2c. Can we collect repro info and logs?

Priya: thanks for the heads up. which cluster / region? any attached support bundle from them? :thinking_face:

alex: Cluster: redwood-dedicated-us-west-2, pool: inference-pool-5. Customer said it happened when sending batch of 8 concurrent streaming requests. No bundle yet — asked them for a curl that reproduces it.

Megan: OK. Alex can you get the full request-id list and timestamps? We'll need pod logs + nvidia metrics + node dmesg. Also ask for a curl that streams so we can reproduce client-side. Example to ask them:```bash
curl -i -N -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-ded-1","input":"say hi","max_tokens":64,"stream":true}'
```

alex: sent that exact curl and asked them to include the failing request_id(s) and the timestamp (UTC). They replied with two request IDs: req_3a9f7b2c and req_3a9f7d4e. Timestamps: 2025-11-02T18:07:12Z and 2025-11-02T18:09:03Z.

Oscar: Great. I'll start collecting logs. Running commands on cluster:```bash
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=inference-pool-5 -o name
# then for each pod:
kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --since=30m > /tmp/<pod>-stdout.log
# stream-side logs (if sidecar):
kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> -c sidecar --since=30m > /tmp/<pod>-sidecar.log
```

Oscar: Also capture node-level metrics and GPU state:```bash
# on node (ssh into node): nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE -x > /tmp/nvidia-<node>.xml
# capture top over 60s:
top -b -n 60 > /tmp/top-60s.log
# dmesg tail:
dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.log
```

Priya: Add controller/operator logs too (rollouts or autoscaler might have reacted):```bash
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-operator --since=1h > /tmp/operator.log
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/hpa-controller --since=1h > /tmp/hpa.log || true
```

Megan: We should capture the inference engine debug output (kv-cache and batching info). On the pod look for: /var/log/inference/runtime-debug.log and the runtime metrics endpoint: curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep batch

alex: Customer also pasted a short snippet of the server error they saw in the response: ```json
{"error":"internal_server_error","message":"timeout while waiting for batch"}
```

Oscar: That error suggests queue/backpressure. I'll pull the runtime-debug.log and the /metrics output around those timestamps.

eng-bot: Deploy noticed at 2025-11-02T17:55:00Z new image redwood/inference:v3.2.1 rolled to pool inference-pool-5 (uid: deploy_20251102_175500). No restarts reported in last 30m.

Megan: Good flag. Possible regression with v3.2.1. Oscar, capture pod restart counts:```bash
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=inference-pool-5 -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
```

Oscar: Copying collection checklist to run via automation so we don't miss anything: - pod stdout/stderr (last 60m) - sidecar logs - runtime-debug.log - /metrics dump - nvidia-smi xml - dmesg - node top - kubelet logs - operator + hpa logs - container inspect (image + env) - core dumps if any (checked /var/lib/crash)

Priya: We also need a minimal repro which hits the same path. If they can run the streaming curl and paste both the full curl command and its output (including headers) that helps a lot (we can correlate request_id). Ask them to set header `X-Debug-Request: true` to force request_id echo if their client strips it.

alex: Customer sent a small tarball with logs (sensitive info redacted). I uploaded it to the secure bucket: s3://redwood-support/repro-1769543210/customer-logs.tar.gz (internal access only).

Megan: I'll pull that and start matching timestamps. Oscar, when you have the runtime logs, grep for the request ids:```bash
grep -n "req_3a9f7b2c\|req_3a9f7d4e" /tmp/*runtime-debug.log /tmp/*-stdout.log || true
```

Oscar: Found runtime traces showing backlog spike at 18:06:58Z:```
[2025-11-02T18:06:58Z] INFO batcher: enqueue request=req_3a9f7b2c queue_size=18 max_workers=16
[2025-11-02T18:06:59Z] WARN batcher: queue_delay_ms=8500
[2025-11-02T18:07:12Z] ERROR dispatcher: request=req_3a9f7b2c error=timeout waiting for worker
```

Megan: That matches the customer's error. Looks like queue_size hit > max_workers and backlog timed out. Need to know why workers weren't available — check GPU utilization and whether some pods were pinned to other workloads.

Oscar: nvidia-smi output shows both GPUs at ~22% util but high memory usage (~90%). Memory pressure could be preventing new model shards from loading quickly. Extract from nvidia xml: ```xml
<gpu>
  <utilization>
    <gpu_util>22</gpu_util>
  </utilization>
  <fb_memory_usage>
    <used>31457280</used>
    <total>34917568</total>
  </fb_memory_usage>
</gpu>
```

Priya: High memory utilization + low GPU compute suggests models are resident and pinned; expensive memory operations might block new allocations. Let's also look at OOM or kernel errors in dmesg.

Oscar: dmesg has repeated lines about GPU driver timeouts around 18:06:56Z. Copy:```
drm: hang detected on GPU 0
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

Megan: Oof. That explains timeouts. We should check node stability and any recent driver updates. eng-bot reported no restarts but GPU driver hangs can persist without container restarts. Action items: 1) escalate to infra SRE for node remediation and driver diagnostics, 2) ask customer to retry against a different pool or reduce concurrency to see if repro persists, 3) collect core dump if available.

alex: Escalating to infra-sre now and recommending customer to route to a different pool as a short-term mitigation. Also asked them to try concurrency=2 and report back.

Priya: Thanks team. Please attach the collected bundle to the ticket and include the grep outputs + nvidia xml + dmesg excerpt. I'll mark this as high priority. :white_check_mark:

Megan: I'll open an internal incident for driver hangs and link this thread.

eng-bot: Incident created INC-20251102-09: "GPU driver hangs causing batcher timeouts" linked to thread 1769543210.

alex: closing loop with customer — told them mitigation + next steps. Will update ticket when they confirm retry. :thumbsup:
